transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-12-29
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Sara Patel (Elysium - Head of ML); Jon Rivera (Elysium - Eng Mgr); Priya Singh (Elysium - Security)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated; concerns: eval parity with vLLM/TGI, latency/cost tradeoffs, security/SOC2/KMS, and pilot scope. Agreed to run a parity benchmark and share security artifacts.

Topics: migration compatibility, benchmarking vLLM/TGI, dedicated pricing, private deployment options, SOC2/KMS, rollout timeline

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Liam, our SE. How are you all doing?
[00:12] Sara (Elysium): Doing good, thanks. Sorry for the slight delay, juggling time zones here.
[00:18] Jon (Elysium): All good. We hopped off another sync but ready.
[00:22] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: understand your current stack and pain points, discuss migration paths from OpenAI, talk about dedicated vs hosted vs private, and surface any security/compliance questions. Sound ok?
[00:32] Priya (Elysium): Yep, that works.
[00:38] Liam (Redwood SE): Quick intro from my side — I usually own the benchmarking and deployment patterns. I'll focus on performance/back-end fit and evaluation parity.
[00:45] Sara: Ok, to give context: we use OpenAI for our core generation flows — mainly chat completions and a bit of embeddings for search. Cost has gone up and latency has variability. We're exploring Dedicated to get predictability and lower unit cost. Also we run an in-house inference layer for some experiments using vLLM, but it's not production.
[01:06] Maya: Helpful. When you say "latency variability", are you seeing tail latency spikes or general throughput issues?
[01:12] Jon: Mostly tail spikes during bursts; also cost spikes with sudden usage leading to throttling that hurts SLAs.
[01:20] Sara: And there's a push from ops to move to reserved capacity—predictable monthly spend—so finance can forecast.
[01:27] Liam: Makes sense. On the compatibility side, are you running model weights locally with vLLM/TGI — e.g., Apache TGI or a custom runner?
[01:35] Sara: We're experimenting with vLLM internally for a few models (Mistral-ish variants and some open Llama forks). It's not fully reliable in prod, mainly for dev workloads. We also evaluate Anthropic for some safety-sensitive flows.
[01:48] Liam: Good to know. Two key areas folks usually ask about: 1) model and API compatibility — how much to change prompts/handlers when moving from OpenAI to Redwood endpoints, and 2) eval parity — does the same model and prompt produce comparable responses when running on Redwood Dedicated vs your local vLLM/TGI runner.
[02:06] Maya: maybe I can jump in — Redwood supports OpenAI-compatible request shapes for many common patterns, and we have adapters for chat/completions and embeddings. But there are subtle differences around function calling and tooling sometimes, so we usually do a short eval to catch regressions.
[02:22] Jon: When you say adapters, do we have to change our app code?
[02:26] Liam: Minimal; typically swap the base URL and keys, maybe small param name differences. For more advanced features like function calling, we'll map them 1:1 in most cases. We'll share a migration checklist.
[02:36] Sara: The big concern is the actual output quality parity. Our ML team trusts the current OpenAI outputs and wants to make sure we don't regress.
[02:44] Liam: Right. We recommend an eval harness — run a held-out prompt set and compare embeddings/likelihoods/LLM outputs across OpenAI, your vLLM baseline, and Redwood Dedicated. We'll provide a spreadsheet and scripts we've used before.
[02:59] Maya: We'll include an example set for semantic search and chat prompts. The initial pilot can be limited to a few routes to measure quality and latency.
[03:09] Priya: From security standpoint, we need SOC2, data residency notes, and details on KMS/HSM, and audit logs. Also interested in private deployment options (VPC or on-prem) since some datasets are PII.
[03:22] Maya: We can share SOC2 report and our standard network diagram. For KMS, Redwood Dedicated can integrate with customer-managed KMS in our Private offering; Dedicated in customer VPC is an option too. We'll include a short doc.
[03:34] Jon: Timeline-wise, if we sign up for a pilot, how fast can we get a Dedicated pool to run tests? We frequently need results in two to three weeks.
[03:44] Liam: For a pilot bench it's typically 1-2 weeks to provision a small reserved pool if we have the contract in place. If you need on-prem or VPC, that adds some time for networking and compliance checks — say 2-4 weeks depending on approvals.
[03:58] Sara: Cost — what are the levers we can pull? Batch size, quantization? We saw Redwood Optimize mentioned in your docs.
[04:07] Liam: Exactly. We have model quantization profiles, batching, and KV cache for prefix reuse. Those reduce token cost. Also running smaller model variants for lower cost routes and auto-fallback to cheaper variants under load. We'll provide recommendations once we see your query distribution.
[04:26] Jon: Any examples on throughput we should expect compared to OpenAI?
[04:30] Liam: It depends on model and hardware. For similar latency SLOs, Dedicated with optimized kernels can be 2-4x cheaper on per-token cost compared to hosted, often better than the economics of public APIs at scale. We'll run bench numbers with your payload to show specifics.
[04:46] Sara: You mentioned model variants and fallbacks — how seamless is that? We don't want to ship degrading user experiences.
[04:52] Maya: You can configure rollout policies and canary rules. Redwood Console supports percentage-based rollouts and automatic fallback if latency or error thresholds are exceeded. The idea is to keep UX consistent.
[05:04] Jon: Ok. About vLLM/TGI parity — are there common reasons local runners produce different results? Tokenization? Kernel implementations?
[05:13] Liam: Good questions. Differences can stem from tokenizers, default sampling parameters, numerical precision (quantization), and subtle implementation details in attention kernels. Also older vLLM/TGI configs might not do the same temperature/top-p defaults. For embeddings, even tokenizer mismatch leads to drift. Our eval aims to control for these and identify where changes are needed.
[05:34] Sara: Do you support loading our exact model weights if we provide them, or is this more about using Redwood-curated weights?
[05:41] Liam: On Dedicated/Private, you can bring-your-own-model weights in many cases (subject to license). For hosted, we provide curated models. We'll check license constraints for any proprietary weights.
[05:52] Priya: For KMS and key access, we need to ensure we can rotate keys and that logs show key usage. Is that available in Dedicated?
[05:59] Maya: Yes, Dedicated + Private integrations support customer-managed KMS and we surface audit logs for key usage in the console. We'll include the exact retention windows and format in the docs.
[06:11] Jon: Any limitations on sequence length or request shapes we should watch for? We do a lot of long-context summarization and sometimes need 8k+ tokens.
[06:20] Liam: Our runtime supports extended contexts, but performance characteristics change; kernel selection and memory footprint matter. For long-context use cases we recommend specific hardware and batching configs. We'll capture your workload distribution and recommend profiles.
[06:33] Sara: Ok, let's talk about the pilot scope — we'd like to validate: 1) functional parity on 500 representative prompts, 2) latency SLO of p95 < 350ms for chat turn, and 3) cost delta targets. Is that reasonable?
[06:47] Liam: Totally reasonable. We'd ask for sample prompts and a baseline dataset. We'll run A/B on your prompts against OpenAI, your vLLM runner, and Redwood Dedicated.
[06:57] Maya: We'll need a sign-off on data access and an NDA if there are sensitive prompts — is that needed?
[07:03] Sara: We have the NDA in place with Redwood, but Priya will confirm internal OK for sample export.
[07:09] Priya: I'll check, yes. Also, how do you handle deletion or redaction of logs for PII?
[07:15] Liam: For Dedicated/Private deployments, you can configure retention. We also have token-level redaction hooks and can disable transcript storage for certain routes. We'll include details.
[07:27] Jon: Are there customers who migrated from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated? Any references?
[07:33] Maya: Yes, we recently helped several customers — I'll share short case studies and a benchmark spreadsheet. One reference did a 60% per-token cost reduction at scale while meeting latency SLOs.
[07:43] Sara: Nice. For metrics, we also need to instrument user-perceived latency — client-side times. Does Redwood provide SDK hooks?
[07:50] Liam: We provide tracing hooks and can include sample middleware for capturing client-to-response times. Console shows route-level metrics.
[07:59] Jon: About function calling — our current app uses OpenAI function calling heavily. How compatible is that?
[08:04] Liam: We support function calling semantics; there may be small differences in how we return structured JSON. We'll validate during the pilot and map edge cases.
[08:14] Sara: On the model side, you mentioned quantization profiles — do you lose quality often when moving to 4-bit?
[08:21] Liam: Quality drop depends on model family. For some models, 4-bit with awareness of outlier detection preserves quality well; for others we recommend 8-bit. The eval will quantify BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarities so you can make a decision.
[08:37] Maya: Quick note — we'll provide a recommended config for batch sizes and prefix caching to balance latency and cost.
[08:43] Jon: Let's talk procurement — what's needed to provision Dedicated? Contract, PO, and some telemetry agreement?
[08:50] Maya: Typically we need a signed contract or SOW and a PO for reserved capacity. For pilot we can do a short-term commitment. We'll share a template SOW.
[08:59] Priya: On legal, we need data processing addendum and details on sub-processors.
[09:04] Maya: We'll include the DPA and sub-processor list.
[09:08] Sara: We also want to test failover — if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can Redwood automatically fall back to hosted or a cheaper variant?
[09:18] Liam: Yes, routing policies can fail over to hosted or to a compatible model variant in a different region. That said, failover to hosted may have a cost delta and potentially different latency profile.
[09:30] Jon: Are there rate limits or soft quotas on Dedicated?
[09:33] Liam: Dedicated is reserved, so throughput is predictable; we still have per-route guards but they are configurable per-customer.
[09:41] Sara: For benchmarks, can you run tests using our real payloads (i.e., anonymized)? We want apples-to-apples.
[09:48] Liam: Yes, anonymized payloads are ideal. We'll run your prompts through the harness. If you can share a sanitized set, we'll kick off.
[09:56] Maya: Anything else from the team?
[09:58] Priya: One more security Q: Do you have attestation for HSM-backed KMS for Private deployments?
[10:05] Liam: For Private + on-prem we can integrate with customer HSMs; we have attestation docs we'll share.
[10:12] Sara: Ok, I think that's the main list.
[10:15] Maya: Great — I'll recap next steps at the end. For now Liam, can you walk through a proposed benchmarking plan?
[10:23] Liam: Sure. Short version: we'll run comparative runs across three targets — OpenAI production key, your vLLM local runner, and Redwood Dedicated. Metrics: token cost, p50/p95 latency, output similarity (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine), and function-calling success. We'll provide scripts to reproduce. We'll also test quantized variants to measure quality impact.
[10:46] Jon: How do you compute embedding similarity? Cosine on pooled vectors?
[10:49] Liam: Typically cosine on the embedding vectors with a ranking evaluation for retrieval tasks. We can give ranked metrics and MRR for search benchmarks.
[10:59] Sara: For the 500 prompt pilot, do you recommend any split between chat and embeddings?
[11:03] Liam: A representative split is best — maybe 60% chat/completion, 30% retrieval/embeddings, 10% edge cases. But we'll adapt to your real distribution.
[11:14] Priya: Also include how logs are stored and retention — we have regulatory constraints for some datasets.
[11:20] Maya: We'll add a retention table in the security packet.
[11:24] Jon: About instrumentation, will we get token-level cost breakdowns per route?
[11:29] Liam: Console surfaces token-level cost per route and per key, yes. You can export for billing reconciliation.
[11:36] Sara: Any concerns about IP or data usage? OpenAI had a clause; we need guarantees data isn't used to train models.
[11:44] Maya: For Dedicated and Private, customer data is isolated and not used for training; we'll include the policy in the DPA.
[11:51] Jon: For the pilot, what does the onboarding look like? Sandbox keys? SDKs?
[11:56] Liam: We'll provide sandbox endpoints and SDK samples for Node/Python, plus a deployment doc. For Dedicated pilot we can provision a small pool and a test key.
[12:07] Sara: Any gotchas you see for teams who've attempted this before?
[12:11] Liam: Watch out for tokenization mismatches and default sampling params. Also ensure your integration captures partial streaming responses if you rely on progressive UI.
[12:23] Maya: Ok I'm going to move us to a quick recap and next steps.
[12:27] Maya: Recap — Elysium wants to validate migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated with a 500-prompt pilot focusing on parity and latency; security artifacts requested; pilot expected to run early January pending sample and contract. Action items: we'll send pricing/SOW, Liam will share the benchmark harness, Priya will confirm data access.
[12:45] Sara: That aligns. One more question: what's the SLA on model upgrades/rollbacks? We need predictable versioning.
[12:52] Liam: You can pin model versions and schedule rollouts. Rollbacks are supported and we keep model version history.
[12:59] Priya: Ok, I'll await the SOC2 and network diagram.
[13:02] Maya: We'll send those today.
[13:06] Jon: Can we earmark a technical deep dive — say next week — to run a small smoke benchmark?
[13:12] Maya: Absolutely. I'll propose times. Liam, any constraints?
[13:15] Liam: Week of Jan 5 works for me. I can run an initial bench and show parity scripts.
[13:21] Sara: Great. Thank you both.
[13:24] Maya: Thanks everyone. End call.

Notes on transcript quality: Auto-transcription had a few mis-heard proper nouns (e.g., model family names) and occasional punctuation issues. Links referenced during the call: Pricing deck: https://redwood.example.com/decks/dedicated-pricing (shared after call); Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/elysium-pilot (to be shared); SOC2 and security packet: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2 (shared).

End of transcript.
